## Current same-object ACL repair candidate

Head `19d2fdfcaefbb41cdf2a72754d695d4b47cb3f14`, tree `17ac791ce156d05d4d1cd13cddf9184e528293a1`, parent `7e0b2303ed0242d83bf56202e8ffb17f5c856186`. **Draft; B11 remains OPEN. This two-path source has not yet executed on Windows.**

The preceding original whole target ran on the actual primary `eed4d6` plus diagnostic `7e0b230` merge and ended with **143 passed / 10 failed / 2 original ignored**. Two directory repairs still failed at ReOpenFile with OS 5; the purported no-WRITE_DAC host control unexpectedly acquired the handle. These observed endpoints motivate the change; the underlying kernel/access-check cause has not been uniquely established.

### Changes

- Preserve the original READ_CONTROL query and complete-deny early return. Only an actual repair opens an existing path with READ_CONTROL, WRITE_DAC and FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES.
- Keep the original query handle alive; reject a final reparse point and require exact volume serial plus all 128 file-ID bits to match before the unchanged handle-based ACL setter can run. Unsupported/zero IDs fail closed.
- Establish the existing no-WRITE_DAC control with an owned file DACL and a new privileges-disabled token impersonating only the synchronous test thread. Verify READ_CONTROL and attribute access first, require the actual CreateFileW OS 5 endpoint, retain all six original assertions, and revert before original DACL restoration on normal/error/panic paths.
- Add one physical file-and-directory replacement control using the same production mutation function. Neither object may change after identity refusal; the retained original must remain repairable by its new name.

Exactly **2 files, 265 additions / 36 deletions** differ from the preceding head. All **10,583 leaves** were checked; dependencies, locks, workflow, masks/SIDs, strict-token rules, budgets and all other original tests are unchanged. Actual repairs now additionally require attribute access and supported nonzero IDs and reject final reparse points; these compatibility limits are explicit.

### Validation and next gate

Independent static review `9eecc3a735653f73e72be9b64e9b055aca519fad` accepted the exact two sources. It checked the installed windows-sys 0.52 API shapes/current features, owned-token/thread restoration, original assertions and eight isolated Git application/reversal checks. Root independently read both full changes and verified the actual Git tree. **These are source checks, not native compilation or execution.**

The unchanged Windows workflow already triggers on both paths and will run the unfiltered original target. Its expected roster is 156 including the one new control; every original failure must remain visible. The separately prepared identity-check-removal counterfactual is **NOT_RUN** and is not being counted as an effective negative control. A passing ACL repair would still leave strict-token outside deletion, ordinary-host prerequisites, finite ambient read/loader and descendant lifetime to resolve.

<details>
<summary>Preserved earlier candidates and complete original Windows outcomes</summary>

## Current ACL repair candidate — 2026-11-05 16:40 UTC

Head `7e0b2303ed0242d83bf56202e8ffb17f5c856186` (tree `3de59a6aa185b13c8758bff3e8fbc530edcef307`), parent `3a407dde2727de2176b02d3cb2c3883fbb771f60`. **B11 remains OPEN. The original whole target has now failed with 143 passed / 10 failed / 2 existing ignored.**

The preceding native run reached all eight mechanism rows but ended with 140 passed / 13 failed / 2 ignored. Those failures include four ACL API errors, one actual strict-token outside deletion, one ordinary-host matrix prerequisite failure before restricted-token construction, one obsolete legacy error-text assertion, and six subsequent process-mutex poison failures. They are not thirteen independent security conclusions.

This commit changes exactly four paths (15 additions / 8 deletions):

- Request `READ_CONTROL | WRITE_DAC` when reopening the same retained object for an ACL repair. The read-only query and complete-deny no-op remain unchanged.
- Keep the existing physical no-WRITE_DAC control aligned with that exact requested access.
- Require the actual typed `PermissionDenied` / OS error 5 in the legacy refusal fixture, retaining the exact outer protected path and proof that no child spawned.
- Add only those three Rust paths to the existing probe workflow's path triggers. Its runner, whole target, command, budget and archive behavior remain unchanged.

Both independent static reviews accepted this candidate for original Windows validation. The directory `ReOpenFile` error 5 cause remains unproved. Token flags/SIDs, policy masks, strict-token assertions and all eight original probe rows remain unchanged. No passing whole-target result is predicted.

The actual generated merge `582f5315f4f632444ae3782d9381f69ed1ae555d` has parents [`eed4d6bb61b789b19f60facc79f9e031765fa4c9`, `7e0b2303ed0242d83bf56202e8ffb17f5c856186`] and tree `1718e3e2235b875320f366d03cf796e2a4e92281`. All 10,585 leaves were independently compared: the merge contains the published primary 14-path update plus this diagnostic source exactly. An immediately returned PR base_sha still showed 5b; the actual Git parents resolve that stale metadata. The completed job attests this exact checkout, tree and the expected source leaves; source status is clean before and after.

### Actual original Windows result, 2026-11-05 16:52:59 UTC

[Run 42066891449 / job 127383345954](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/actions/runs/42066891449/job/127383345954) completed with the original Bazel exit 3. The two disjoint harness partitions total **143 PASS / 10 FAIL / 2 existing ignored**; these are not retries.

Three original cases now directly pass: partial-read deny repair and the legacy capture/session refusal-before-spawn cases. Remaining failures comprise two directory ReOpenFile errors (OS 5), one physical no-WRITE_DAC control whose prerequisite unexpectedly grants the reopened handle, one real strict-token outside deletion, two ordinary-host matrix prerequisites before restricted-subject testing, and four subsequent mutex-poison failures. No cause is asserted for the directory failure until verified.

Root verified the complete 14-member ZIP against the fresh official artifact digest, all original failure blocks, source leaves and clean pre/post status. Six mechanism JSON rows are parseable. The host/medium and current_strict/medium rows are interleaved in original stdout and remain unrepaired; this differs from the preceding run. All eight restoration/finalization rows are complete: 80 owned objects, 54 survivors, 26 deleted/pending, zero restoration errors, no descendants spawned. A completed probe still does not qualify production loader, finite ambient read or descendant lifetime.

The next repair must preserve the original no-op and negative assertions while proving same-object identity for directory ACL mutation and establishing an actually unprivileged no-WRITE_DAC control. The separate strict-token escape remains open. Complete originals and root receipt are retained. No manual rerun or cancellation.

<details>
<summary>Preserved prior evidence and publication history</summary>

## Why

B11 remains open: the original Windows strict controls observed successful outside file/directory deletion under broad identity ACEs. We need physical evidence to distinguish mandatory-integrity behavior, DELETE_CHILD access, and the read-capability alternative before changing production permissions.

## Changes

This diagnostic Draft is based on `5b6331250ff459033bd44d1a95daec70131277cc`, independently of the pending Core/musl candidate. The initial three commits added the four-path diagnostic, and a fourth commit fixes the actual Windows compile prerequisite. The PR now changes five paths:

- Add test-only helpers that capture, set, verify and restore labels on newly created owned objects using retained handles.
- Add an eight-row physical probe: four token subjects × Medium/Low outside-object labels. It records effective thread token state, same-descriptor AccessCheck results, and real read/write/create/file-delete/directory-delete results.
- Run the original outer Windows sandbox unit target in a dedicated Windows/MSVC job. Preserve the original 120-minute budget, assertions, test selection, retries and Bazel exit code; retain complete observations and original target logs/XML.

The production token implementation is byte-for-byte unchanged apart from a 78-byte `cfg(test)` module registration. The original three strict controls and two four-cell controls are unchanged.

## Validation and limits

- The complete four-path tree was independently fetched and compared with all 10,580 base leaves: one changed existing file and three additions; every other leaf is unchanged.
- Static patch reconstruction, YAML/Bash syntax, Windows API bindings and an independent full review passed.
- The first actual Windows run (42049112832 / job 127320081049) reached the original Rust 1.95 target and failed before any test: eight E0659 errors in the existing delete_permission_tests.rs module. The complete original failure is retained.
- The new commit adds only an explicit import of the parent's existing pretty_assertions::assert_eq macro; removing that line reproduces the exact original file. All eight assertions are unchanged. Its path is added to the same diagnostic workflow trigger. The corrected source still needs actual Windows compilation and execution.
- The probe requires valid fixtures, inside positive controls, original reads and restoration. Outside denial is recorded without inventing an expected result. **Probe PASS does not close B11.**
- This probe does not start descendants and does not qualify loader, IPC, backend, Job descendants, production Root/Current or ambient-read closure.

The actual original target result, six named-case reachability, all eight observation rows, completion marker, cache/skip/attempt details and restoration must be inspected before choosing a production fix.

## Fixed review inputs

- Full four-path patch: `f8869774509a4226328bc4dc28243e86a35f8779`
- Manifest: `dfbd4f609afa66239ca2b6d10fd584e882987bf3`
- Independent review: `3f2afcb1df8a905cb348106012454902a2c1c06a`

B11 stays OPEN; this PR is not a merge or release qualification.

Current diagnostic head: `0d65de9bf1e28a7b313a344ebba71ba8378d0f5a`; tree `f13680916b9a7f773dcc95e4ce6ee6785021ead4`. The primary product PR #4797 is unchanged.

## Second actual Windows outcome and next diagnostic

The corrected macro compiled and the original tests executed in run 42051179792 / job 127327372905. Original strict tests still failed. The new probe stopped at its initial explicit-label equality gate before any of the eight physical rows; the failure did not include the two compared SDDL values. Commit `c05dc16cc055e58d020d848d2bca0ff04736e7c2` only prints those existing values and owned path before the unchanged exact comparison. It does not change token flags, label APIs, restoration, assertions or budgets. The next result must be inspected before choosing any semantic correction.

Current diagnostic head: `c05dc16cc055e58d020d848d2bca0ff04736e7c2`; tree `6646c0b2670b5877f46b80494c042c9d3fe9ec42`; five commits, five paths. Prior failures remain retained. B11 OPEN.


### Strict label ACE fixture correction

The original c05 job [127336717141](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/actions/runs/42053829668/job/127336717141) compiled and executed the unfiltered original target, then stopped the mechanism probe before its eight physical rows. The observed initial label was `S:AI(ML;;NW;;;ME)` while the explicit template was `S:(ML;;NW;;;ME)`. The unchanged original target still failed (139 passing, 14 failing, 2 ignored across its disjoint libtest partitions).

Commit `3a407dde2727de2176b02d3cb2c3883fbb771f60` changes only the test support module. It requires exactly one valid mandatory-label ACE and compares exact ACE type, inheritance flags, policy mask and all SID bytes. Descriptor ACL control flags remain observed separately. The original descriptor remains held unchanged; surviving objects must restore full owner/group/DACL/label text and exact raw descriptor control/revision. The original physical operations, AccessCheck calls, eight-row assertions, production token flags, target selection and budgets are unchanged.

Static author review `26631a3b242c5a14df89b22de4f6c1a84d3aa904` and independent review `c06ff63c83722832ce03840407c6aef3fd471b4c` are retained. Fresh Windows execution is required. This remains an observation-only diagnostic Draft; B11 and the main product qualification remain open.
